clues.name: 5:45 PM
clues.context: A quarter to six. The light still long, the kitchen getting loud.
clues.inspectorDescription: Late afternoon, by the smell of it. Every kitchen in the world gets busy around now.

clues.name: 6:00 PM
clues.context: Six o'clock sharp. The evening's first appointment.
clues.inspectorDescription: Six sharp. Some appointments in this house are never missed. Almost never.

clues.name: 6:30 PM
clues.context: Half past six. The evening starting to fill up.
clues.inspectorDescription: Half past six. People begin arriving in bunches around then. Allegedly.

clues.name: 6:45 PM
clues.context: A quarter to seven. Golden light, long shadows.
clues.inspectorDescription: A good hour for being seen. Or for hoping nobody is looking.

clues.name: 6:47 PM
clues.context: Two minutes past a quarter to seven. Oddly precise.
clues.inspectorDescription: Machines remember what people round off. This one came off a screen.

clues.name: 7:00 PM
clues.context: Seven o'clock. The single busiest minute this house has ever had.
clues.inspectorDescription: Everyone swears they were somewhere at seven. That is a lot of somewheres for one minute.

clues.name: 7:20 PM
clues.context: Twenty past seven. The evening still on wheels.
clues.inspectorDescription: The late traffic. By then the hallway had heard it all before.

clues.name: 8:00 PM
clues.context: Eight o'clock. Full dark.
clues.inspectorDescription: The one moment this whole house agrees on - which is exactly what bothers me about it.

clues.name: 8:15 PM
clues.context: A quarter past eight. After this, nobody goes anywhere.
clues.inspectorDescription: The moment the doors stopped opening. Everything that matters happened before it.

clues.name: Lockdown
clues.context: Officer Reyes sealed the mansion - full perimeter, his seal on every door. Nobody in or out since.
clues.inspectorDescription: Doors sealed. Officer Reyes does not negotiate. I checked.

clues.name: PR Disaster
clues.context: The Manager, Chip Sterling, is furious that a missing animal is generating terrible press for his client.
clues.inspectorDescription: Chip Sterling hates animals and loves percentages. Strong feelings. No evidence either way.

clues.name: Crew Arrivals
clues.context: The sign-in book logs the whole household coming and going all afternoon - and then the film crew's column begins, hurried and overlapping.
clues.inspectorDescription: Wexler first. Then the handler plus one bird. Then the socialite. And then a crew column too sloppy to count. My eyes glazed twice.

clues.name: Rumble Downstairs
clues.context: Derek heard something heavy rumble through the house below - the entrance hall, then the living room - earlier this evening. He assumed the dinner cart.
clues.inspectorDescription: Wheels, somewhere under the floorboards. He didn't look. Could have been the dinner service. Could have been anything on wheels.

clues.name: Squawk Through Headphones
clues.context: Even through brand-new noise-canceling headphones, Derek heard the bird scream. His takeaway: wherever Rudebeak went, he was still around - loud and alive.
clues.inspectorDescription: Three hundred dollars of silence, and one squawk cut straight through it. Derek finds that comforting. I find it interesting.

clues.name: Manifest Entry
clues.context: The delivery manifest logs two equipment cases into the east wing.
clues.inspectorDescription: Two cases, east wing. The manifest is very sure about the hour and very quiet about everything else.

clues.name: Scrawled Signature
clues.context: The 7:00 PM cases were signed in with a hurried scribble. Every other entry on the manifest has a readable name beside it.
clues.inspectorDescription: Florist, legible. Housekeeping, legible. Grip department, legible. Two heavy cases: a scribble with a tail. Only one entry did not want to be read.

clues.name: Second Rumble
clues.context: Derek finally counted: the heavy rumble downstairs came twice this evening. Same weight, same wheels - and the kitchen only ran one cart.
clues.inspectorDescription: Two identical rumbles, one cart run on the roster. Derek filed both under 'not my problem'.

clues.name: Smell of Cable Grease
clues.context: Rosa swears the bedroom wing smelled of soup and cable grease that night. The soup was hers.
clues.inspectorDescription: Kitchens know their smells. Soup, hers. Cable grease, somebody else's - a workshop smell in a food hallway, and it did not come off her cart.

clues.name: 'The Cases Are EMPTY'
clues.context: Nobody told the Sound Guy what was inside the hidden cases. He said it himself - empty, both of them - before anyone asked.
clues.inspectorDescription: I never said a word about what was in them. Neither did anyone else. He counted them for me anyway.

clues.name: Settled Feathers
clues.context: The feathers beneath the cage lie perfectly flat. Whatever happened at this cage happened long before anyone started screaming.
clues.inspectorDescription: Feathers take time to settle. These are flat as Tuesday. This cage has been quiet for hours.

clues.name: Sound-Proof Cases
clues.context: Two big black road cases, stashed behind the garden shed under a hastily thrown tarp. Heavy latches, thick foam lining.
clues.inspectorDescription: Foam-lined and heavy-latched. I pressed an ear against one for science. Nothing. Which proves nothing. Which is the point.

clues.name: Derek the Husband
clues.context: Derek bought top-of-the-line noise-canceling headphones the day before the bird vanished - a man pushed to the edge by 5 AM squawks, with a spare audio cable in the box.
clues.inspectorDescription: New headphones, a spare cable, an ultimatum in his own handwriting. He solved his bird problem somehow. The question is which way.

clues.name: Derek's Ultimatum
clues.context: A handwritten note from Derek to his wife: 'Viv - Rudebeak woke me up at 5AM. AGAIN. Do SOMETHING about that bird or I will. I am past asking nicely.'
clues.inspectorDescription: Derek wanted the bird handled - in writing. His solution arrived in a headphone box. Somebody else's didn't.

clues.name: Derek's Headphones
clues.context: A freshly opened box of top-of-the-line noise-canceling headphones, a spare audio cable still coiled inside. The receipt is dated yesterday.
clues.inspectorDescription: Ordered the day before the shoot, audio cable and all. The bird drove him to it. His solution was at least legal.

clues.name: Service Tray
clues.context: A collected dinner tray sits on the dresser - soup bowls emptied, dinner delivered and cleared on schedule.
clues.inspectorDescription: Soup happened here. The cart came, the cart went. I checked the bowls for further secrets. None. Shame.

clues.name: The Squawk
clues.context: Vivienne Vale is certain she heard Rudebeak squawk - late, loud, and unmistakable.
clues.inspectorDescription: She knows that screech anywhere, she says. Nobody actually SAW the bird after dinner.

clues.name: Broken Latch
clues.context: The cage latch was forced open with something flat and strong.
clues.inspectorDescription: Forced open with something flat and strong. And the feathers beneath the cage have long since settled.

clues.name: Hidden Speaker
clues.context: A thin cable slips out from behind the living room couch; taped to the couch frame sits a small wireless speaker.
clues.inspectorDescription: Taped where nobody would look unless they were cat-height. The cable slips away behind the wainscoting.

clues.name: Dropped Glove
clues.context: A single canvas gardening glove lies beneath the birdcage stand, smelling of mulch.
clues.inspectorDescription: One canvas glove, garden-flavored, indoors on parquet. Gloves come in pairs. This one has lost its partner.

clues.name: Lemon Polish Cloth
clues.context: A lemon-oil polishing cloth is draped over the cage stand rail - the housekeeping kind.
clues.inspectorDescription: Lemon oil, fresh. The whole stand gleams. Somebody dusts this cage daily, and close enough to reach right in.

clues.name: Documentary Camera
clues.context: A film crew camera, recording all day - but aimed at the chaise for Vivienne's interviews. The cage sits just outside its frame.
clues.inspectorDescription: Recording all day, pointed at the wrong thing. Four hundred hours of Vivienne's good side, and not one frame of the cage.

clues.name: Vocab Ledger
clues.context: A booklet of phrases taught to Rudebeak. The entry for 'garbage slop' is crossed out with 'MAID'S FAULT' written next to it.
clues.inspectorDescription: Vivienne blames Rosa for teaching Rudebeak the insult. Somebody in this house was keeping score.

clues.name: Ruined Takes
clues.context: A session log by the mixer: 'TAKE 47 - RUINED. BIRD. AGAIN.' Pages and pages of them.
clues.inspectorDescription: Forty-seven ruined takes. The handwriting gets angrier with every page.

clues.name: Wexler's Ratings
clues.context: Director Wexler sees the crisis as a documentary opportunity. He is thrilled.
clues.inspectorDescription: Not grief. Ratings. Suspiciously thrilled - or just a vulture with a lens?

clues.name: Audio Cable
clues.context: An audio cable runs from the mixing board and disappears into the wall.
clues.inspectorDescription: It leaves the mixing board and vanishes into the wall, heading west. Cables don't usually hide behind wainscoting.

clues.name: Sound Guy: D. Marsh
clues.context: The Sound Guy's name badge identifies him as D. Marsh.
clues.inspectorDescription: Badge says D. Marsh. He said 'nice cat' in a voice half an octave too high. His headphones aren't plugged into anything.

clues.name: Shot List
clues.context: The Director's shot list shows 'Rudebeak reaction shot' was cancelled, with a note in red pen: 'BETTER WITHOUT HIM?'
clues.inspectorDescription: He cancelled the bird's segment. And then wrote a very suspicious note about it in red pen.

clues.name: Rosa the Maid
clues.context: Rosa has a temper, a cleaver, and access to every room in the house.
clues.inspectorDescription: A temper, a motive, and a master key. And nobody watches the kitchen between courses.

clues.name: Insulted Cooking
clues.context: The bird publicly insulted Rosa's cooking. She wrote it down. She drew a skull next to it.
clues.inspectorDescription: The bird called her paella garbage slop. In front of guests. She drew a skull. In pen.

clues.name: Rosa's Paella
clues.context: Rosa's paella is on the stove. It smells extraordinary.
clues.inspectorDescription: For the record: the paella smells incredible. Rudebeak had terrible taste in food criticism.

clues.name: Feathers in the Bin
clues.context: A bin of feathers by the prep counter, next to tonight's roast. Rosa plucks the dinner birds herself.
clues.inspectorDescription: Feathers. In the kitchen of a woman with a list. I looked for a long time. Kitchen-bird feathers. Probably. I am keeping one eye on that bin.

clues.name: Dinner Cart
clues.context: The kitchen duty roster: 'R. - dinner cart to the east wing.' The east wing is where the bedrooms are.
clues.inspectorDescription: Rosa. A heavy cart. The bedroom wing. The plot thickens like a good bechamel.

clues.name: Cages Are Prisons
clues.context: Basil the gardener preaches that animals belong in nature - to hedges, to fountains, to anyone who will listen. A man like that might free a bird on principle.
clues.inspectorDescription: He says it four times an hour, unprompted, to a cat. Principles that loud usually want a witness. Or an alibi.

clues.name: Basil the Gardener
clues.context: Basil believes caged animals should be free. He is trimming the same hedge for the fourth time.
clues.inspectorDescription: 'Animals belong in nature.' Said four times, unprompted, to a cat.

clues.name: Bent Shears
clues.context: The pruning shears show a bend consistent with forcing a metal latch.
clues.inspectorDescription: The bend in these blades fits a forced metal latch the way a paw fits a sunbeam.

clues.name: Evening Feathers
clues.context: Fresh feathers in the bird bath. Rudebeak was in the garden this evening, out of his cage.
clues.inspectorDescription: Fresh and bright, still crisp on the water. He was out here this evening, having a lovely time.

clues.name: Coco's Sighting
clues.context: Coco the Socialite saw someone hauling large black cases through the garden while the light was still good.
clues.inspectorDescription: 'Some crew person,' she says. She was mostly focused on her drink. The cases, though - those she remembers.

clues.name: Pool Selfie
clues.context: A timestamped pool selfie. In the blurry background, a figure hauls large cases along the garden path - and at the frame's edge, someone peeks out from behind the potting shed.
clues.inspectorDescription: The timestamp is exact. The figure is blurry. The cases are not. And behind the shed: one very worried straw hat.

clues.name: Production Schedule
clues.context: The official crew schedule, found crumpled into a ball. Smoothed flat, it assigns D. Marsh to Library audio setup at 7:00 PM.
clues.inspectorDescription: Crew schedule, 7:00 PM: 'D. Marsh - Library (audio setup).' Somebody balled it up and threw it away. Schedules only mean something when people follow them.

clues.name: North Gate Locked
clues.context: Police radio confirms the north garden gate was locked all evening.
clues.inspectorDescription: Locked all evening, confirmed twice on the radio. Nobody left through the garden.

clues.name: Chip's Commission
clues.context: Chip Sterling takes fifteen percent of everything the Star earns - including the bird's documentary fee.
clues.inspectorDescription: He takes fifteen percent of the bird's earnings. A man doesn't kidnap his own commission. Probably.

clues.name: Suspected Bribery
clues.context: Rosa keeps a jar of cat treats labeled 'FOR THE CAT.' If this is a bribe, it is working.
clues.inspectorDescription: She keeps treats. For me. Specifically. I must remain objective. The treats were excellent.

clues.name: Muddy Glove
clues.context: Basil's right glove is caked in fresh mud. He says he was planting bulbs. The flower bed agrees with him. His left hand is bare.
clues.inspectorDescription: Fresh mud, matching the freshly planted bulb bed. One glove working hard. Its partner is nowhere on him.

clues.name: Bright Feather
clues.context: A single bright feather, red fading into blue. It could have blown in from anywhere.
clues.inspectorDescription: One bright feather. The wind carries feathers everywhere. I did not bap it. There were no witnesses either way.

clues.name: Lamp Returns
clues.context: The manifest logs the grip department wheeling lamp returns through the east wing.
clues.inspectorDescription: More wheels in the wing, later than the rest. This hallway was practically a freeway tonight. No wonder nobody looked twice.

clues.name: Household Sign-In
clues.context: The registry lists the whole household by role: Wexler the director, Petra the bird handler, Coco the socialite, staff in since morning.
clues.inspectorDescription: Everyone signs the book. Directors, handlers, socialites, staff. A house this full is never short of suspects.

clues.name: Missed Snack
clues.context: Rudebeak's evening seed bowl sits untouched beside the cage. Petra says he has never once missed it.
clues.inspectorDescription: The bowl is full. The bird is punctual. He was gone before his own supper.

clues.name: Fresh-Turned Flower Bed
clues.context: A flower bed of freshly planted daffodil bulbs, turned over this afternoon - exactly where Basil says he was working.
clues.inspectorDescription: Dug today, planted neatly. Somebody spent the afternoon out here with their hands in the dirt.

clues.name: Boot Prints by the Shed
clues.context: Heavy boot prints press the grass flat behind the potting shed - deep at the toe, like someone carrying weight.
clues.inspectorDescription: Deep at the toe. Whoever stood here was hauling something. Gardeners wear boots. So does a film crew.

clues.name: Wexler the Director
clues.context: Director Wexler has three cameras of footage to review and not a trace of grief. He keeps calling the crisis 'material'.
clues.inspectorDescription: He frames everything with his fingers, including me. A man who profits from drama, surrounded by drama.

clues.name: Unplugged Headphones
clues.context: The Sound Guy's monitoring headphones end a foot short of the mixing board, plugged into nothing at all.
clues.inspectorDescription: He is 'monitoring levels' through a cable that connects to air. Either a genius or a man pretending to work.

clues.name: Ring of House Keys
clues.context: A ring of house keys jingles at Rosa's apron - the housekeeping set. It opens every room in the mansion.
clues.inspectorDescription: Every door in the house, one apron. Anyone who borrowed that ring for an hour could go anywhere they liked.

clues.name: Herb Run
clues.context: The duty roster logs a herb run in from the garden, initialed 'B.'
clues.inspectorDescription: B. came in from the garden with the herbs. The roster does not say what else he passed on the way.

clues.name: Straw Hat in Frame
clues.context: At the very edge of Coco's 6:47 photo, someone in a straw hat peeks out from behind the potting shed.
clues.inspectorDescription: Hiding, not working. Whoever wears that hat watched the cases roll by and told nobody.

clues.name: Abandoned Spritz
clues.context: Coco's spritz sits abandoned on the chaise, warm through - poured for sunset, forgotten the moment the cases rolled past.
clues.inspectorDescription: Warm all the way through. She was out here well before the light went. Bored, and therefore reliable.

clues.name: Rudebeak the Macaw
clues.context: The missing macaw himself: blue-and-gold, world-famous, with a documentary deal and opinions about everyone in this house.
clues.inspectorDescription: Famous, rude, and missing. Birds this loud do not usually vanish this quietly. That is the whole case, really.

clues.name: Still Inside
clues.context: Officer Reyes's professional read: nothing has left the property since his seal went on. Whoever took the bird is still on the grounds.
clues.inspectorDescription: Sealed doors, locked gate. Everything I am looking for is somewhere under this roof. Convenient. Also ominous.

clues.name: Officer Reyes
clues.context: The officer holding the front door: unbribable, unhurried, and quietly taking the cat seriously.
clues.inspectorDescription: He scratched my ear exactly once and pretended it never happened. We are partners now. He will figure it out eventually.

clues.name: Does Not Add Up
clues.context: Reyes's verdict on the sign-in book: hurried arrivals, sloppy signatures - somebody's evening in that book does not add up.
clues.inspectorDescription: He would not say whose. 'Your department,' he said. I have a department now.

clues.name: Chip Sterling
clues.context: The Manager: a phone welded to his ear, fifteen percent of everything, and a client brand to protect at all costs.
clues.inspectorDescription: He practices his concerned face in the hall mirror. It still needs work. The worry underneath it looks real, though.

clues.name: Suspiciously Unanimous
clues.context: Reyes's canvass came back unanimous: every person in this house heard the same squawk at the same minute. Nobody saw the bird.
clues.inspectorDescription: Fifteen years on the job, he says, and honest witnesses never agree that neatly. I am inclined to trust the man on this.

clues.name: Vivienne Vale
clues.context: The Movie Star: grieving in couture, certain of what she heard, and never far from a camera.
clues.inspectorDescription: She held me up like a press photo and called my eyes kind. The grief is real. The angles are better.

clues.name: Petra the Handler
clues.context: The Bird Handler: precise, professional, and worried sick behind the procedure. She knows Rudebeak's routine to the minute.
clues.inspectorDescription: She reads animals for a living and nodded at me like a colleague. Correct on both counts.

clues.name: Spent Earplugs
clues.context: A nightstand drawer rattling with used foam earplugs - months of failed defenses against 5 AM wake-up squawks.
clues.inspectorDescription: He tried the cheap way first, many times over. The three hundred dollar escalation was thoroughly earned.

finalSolveSentence: He was inside by [WHEN] - a full half hour before his own call. The snatch was caught on camera at [WHEN], and by [WHEN] the cargo was rolling right past the bedrooms. [WHO] hid Rudebeak inside the [WHAT], kept the house believing with the [HOW], and it all comes back to the [WHY].
